stories.headline: Strong 7.0-magnitude earthquake hits Tibet’s Baqen County in China
stories.title: Strong 7.0-magnitude earthquake hits Tibet’s Baqen County in China
stories.summary: The earthquake struck at 10.33 pm local time, with its epicentre recorded at 32.40 degrees north latitude and 93.79 degrees east longitude.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Tibet’s Nagqu City on Thursday night, according to China’s earthquake monitoring agency.
An earthquake of magnitude 7.0 struck China's Tibet Autonomous Region on Thursday, the China Earthquake Networks Centre (CENC) said.
There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage following the quake, which hit Baqen County of Nagqu City around 10.33 PM local time.
The epicentre was monitored at 32.40 degrees north latitude and 93.79 degrees east longitude.
The quake struck at a depth of 10 km, state-run Xinhua news agency reported.
The Tibetan Plateau is known to be prone to powerful earthquakes as it sits right over the place where the Eurasian and Indian tectonic plates meet, often colliding with huge force.

stories.headline: Election petitions cannot be filed merely on the basis of videos downloaded from internet: Madras High Court
stories.title: Election petitions cannot be filed merely on the basis of videos downloaded from internet: Madras High Court
stories.summary: Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan says there must also be independent documentary material to establish returned candidate’s alleged involvement in corrupt practices
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: An election petition cannot be filed merely on the basis of videos downloaded from the internet without there being any independent documentary material to establish the returned candidate’s alleged involvement in corrupt practices, the Madras High Court has held.

Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan passed the ruling while rejecting an election petition filed by a DMK advocate’s wing office-bearer, in his capacity as a voter, challenging the victory of AIADMK former Minister C.Ve.
Shanmugam from Mailam Assembly constituency in the 2026 general elections.
Mr. Shanmugam had won the seat by securing 82,533 votes as against 52,312 votes secured by his nearest rival candidate.
A. Vijay Niranjan of TVK.
However, P. Kamalakkannan of Tindivanam had filed the election petition accusing the MLA of having indulged in electoral corrupt practices.
The petitioner alleged that the returned candidate had paid cash of ₹1,000 each to several voters in Kongarapattu village besides issuing coupons promising payment of ₹2,000 each to every voter.
He relied upon video recordings to contend that the money was paid with the consent of the MLA.
On the other hand, urging the court to reject the election petition, the MLA said, the petitioner had failed to disclose to the court that he was a member of the DMK advocate’s wing.
The MLA also stated that the videos had been downloaded from the internet without ascertaining their authenticity and reliability.
After hearing both sides, the judge wrote: “The election petitioner had no personal knowledge of any of the allegations leveled in the election petition.
The allegations were made solely on the basis of information received from certain persons and a videograph downloaded from the internet...

stories.headline: Incumbent president Swami Sathchidananda loses election at Sivagiri Sree Narayana Dharma Sanghom Trust in Keralam
stories.title: Incumbent president Swami Sathchidananda loses election at Sivagiri Sree Narayana Dharma Sanghom Trust in Keralam
stories.summary: However, the existing panel led by him secured a majority in the election, giving the outgoing administration an advantage in determining the trust’s future leadership
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Swami Sathchidananda, the incumbent president of the Sree Narayana Dharma Sanghom Trust at Sivagiri Madhom, suffered defeat in the elections to the trust’s governing body for the 2026-31 term.
However, the existing panel led by him secured a majority in the election, giving the outgoing administration an advantage in determining the trust’s future leadership.
The elections for the 11-member governing board was held, with retired District Judge K. Viswanathan Nair as the returning officer.
As many as 55 of the 56 members eligible to vote participated in the process.
Swami Sathchidananda received only 17 votes.
Nonetheless, six members of the existing governing body were re-elected.

Those re-elected include the incumbent general secretary Swami Shubhangananda (29 votes), Swami Rithambarananda (24), Swami Yogananda Theerthar (24), Swami Anapekshananda (26), Swami Dharmachaithanya (26), and Swami Nithyaswaroopananda (26).
Swami Ambikananda (31), Swami Guruprakasam (28), Swami Vishuddhananda (28), Swami Sharadananda (26) and Swami Sandranandapuri (24) are the other elected members.
The newly elected board will decide who succeeds Swami Sathchidananda as the president of the trust, along with the other office-bearers.

stories.summary: Dr. Sandeep Mahajan: Engineering the Future of Sustainable LivingThe future of housing belongs to leaders who dare to rethink Construction. Dr. Sandeep Mahajan, Founder of Vrisa Innovation Limited is advancing sustainable modular construction for a rapidly evolving India. Established in 2010, Vrisa transforms buildings through CMS-Composite Modular Structures, foldable and expandable prefab homes, and V-PODS-ready-to-use space capsules introduced in 2024.With over 200 structures across India, the company combines rapid delivery, customization, and environmental responsibility. Its achievements include the Udyog Bharati Award, Bhartiya Udyog Ratna Award, Pune Udyog Bhushan Award, Most Trusted Company recognition, and an Honorary Doctorate in Sustainable Construction.Recognised among leading prefab and modular construction companies, Dr. Mahajan champions future-ready sustainable living. As Vrisa expands globally, his leadership remains focused on reshaping construction through innovation, sustainability, and trust.Rohaan Patill: Building the Next Global Trading and Energy Powerhouse In trading, team and trust are everything.Founder and Director of Ace Raysons Global Group and Ace Raysons Helios, Rohaan drives agri-commodity and petroleum trading with government-owned oil corporations, alongside strategic data centre and solar acquisitions.His core team: execution led by Harsh Tripathi, Pankaj Mundada and Saanjay Waje; finance by Rochelle D’Souza, Udit Sachdeva, Manish Kaushik and Arjun Sharma; crude and LPG by former HPCL crude trading head Subhabrata Tripathi, former IOCL CGM Rashmi Dhingra and Rohit Kumar; shipping and logistics by Capt. Its client portfolio includes Zomato, Blinkit and Flipkart.Recognised by Industry Outlook as a “Top Company in Generator Rental Services – 2026,” Excel Generators continues to strengthen its service capabilities, guided by reliability, accountability and customer trust.Crest Architects: Defying Gravity, Redefining PossibilitiesAt an age when most architecture students were translating ideas onto paper, Ar. At 20, they began their journey with Floating Walls, a multi-award-winning project that laid the foundation for Crest Architects and a vision unafraid to challenge convention.Since its inception, Crest has pushed the boundaries of architectural expression, carving a distinct identity through cantilevers, structural ingenuity, and sensitivity to context. Each project explores the interplay of architecture, engineering, and human experience, creating spaces that are visually compelling yet grounded in their surroundings.Today, Crest Architects is a sought-after practice, recognised for its architectural language.For Crest, architecture is an experience to be lived, an emotion to be remembered, and a relationship between people and spaces.Bhagyashri Varma, Founder- Noesis Service ConsultantsTrained as an architect but drawn to the systems that work silently behind every wall, Ar. Bhagyashri Varma built Noesis Service Consultants on a simple conviction: that a building’s services belong in its first sketch, never its afterthoughts. Too often, she argues, engineering is squeezed into spaces already drawn, leaving lowered ceilings and costly redesigns during execution, so her firm weaves MEP, fire and life safety, sustainability and compliance into the earliest stages of planning instead.As Indian cities grow denser and every square metre is chased for revenue, her case is that shafts, plant rooms and service corridors are not lost space but performance space, a distinction the buildings of the next decade cannot afford to ignore.Dr. Parth Rana, Medical Director , Netralaya Super Speciality Eye HospitalDr. Parth Rana, a retina and ocular trauma surgeon who completed India's first Ocular Trauma Fellowship, has helped reshape the economics of eye surgery. He has also chosen to forgo royalties so the lenses stay affordable.As medical director of Ahmedabad's Netralaya Super Speciality Eye Hospital, he has brought specialists in retina, glaucoma, cornea, ocular oncology and more under one roof, alongside Gujarat's first 3D Eye surgery system, Ultra wide field Retina imaging System, ultra wide field OCT and many other latest diagnostic equipment first in Gujarat so none of the Gujarat eye patients have to go out of the state to get their eyes treated. The hospital plans a nine-storey centre and free care through government schemes, with the hope that no patient will ever need to leave Gujarat for eye care.Gautham Nekkanti: Strengthening India’s Defence Capabilities Beyond GPSWhen GPS fails, national security cannot afford to. Under his leadership, GarudaNav Core has achieved Technology Readiness Level 7, recorded over 100 cumulative flight-test hours and completed a GPS-denied UAV mission at the Indian Air Force’s Dronathon in September 2026.By combining personal conviction with indigenous innovation, Nekkanti is helping strengthen India’s strategic autonomy and build the next generation of assured navigation systems.Sahil Sanjay Jaggi | Shaping India’s Global FutureSahil Sanjay Jaggi, Director of World One Import Export LLP, is a forward-thinking entrepreneur strengthening India’s presence in global commerce. Leading diversified international trade across ethnic wear, accessories, handicrafts, FMCG, chemicals and industrial products, his company operates as a global sourcing and consolidation partner, connecting Indian manufacturers with international markets. With manufacturing partnerships supporting leading retail stores worldwide, he is building a stronger bridge between Indian capabilities and global demand. stories.headline: Ladakh administration defends in HC cancellation of land allotment to Wangchuk’s institute
stories.title: Ladakh administration defends in HC cancellation of land allotment to Wangchuk’s institute
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 22: The Ladakh administration has defended cancelling land allotment to Sonam Wangchuk's institute, citing the activist's "disregard for the law", and said the allotment automatically lapsed due to unpaid dues and an unexecuted lease deed. In an affidavit filed in the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, the administration maintained that the 40-year lease allotment covering 1,076 kanals and 1 marla of land at Phyang Thang had "lapsed by operation of law" on May 5, 2019, due to the Himalayan Institute of Alternative Learning (HIAL)'s failure to execute a lease deed or deposit mandatory land premiums within the stipulated one-year period. The affidavit running into 136 pages was filed by Leh Deputy Commissioner and CEO of LAHDC, Romil Singh Donk, in response to HIAL's writ petition challenging the August 21, 2025, cancellation order of leased land to the institute. The affidavit said the writ petition is "misconceived, devoid of merit, and barred by delay and laches" and made it clear that the original allotment order issued on May 5, 2018, was conditional and explicitly stated that the lease would be deemed cancelled if the allottee failed to execute the deed within a year. The administration asserted that HIAL never deposited a single rupee towards land premium or ground rent and failed to secure formal possession through the Tehsildar as mandated. Furthermore, the Higher Education Department of UT Ladakh certified in October 2026 that HIAL is not a recognised university, nor are its courses affiliated with the University of Ladakh or other statutory bodies, violating the core objective of setting up an alternative university. Bringing other context before the court, the affidavit highlighted the past conduct of HIAL's founder Wangchuk and his organisation, the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL), and said that SECMOL has occupied 124 kanals of state land at Phey for over three decades without formal allotment or payment of an assessed Rs 80 lakh premium. The affidavit also references the violent protests in Leh in September 2025, which led to Union Home Ministry's intervention, the cancellation of SECMOL's FCRA registration, and Wangchuk's brief detention under the National Security Act prior to its revocation in March 2026, as part of a consistent pattern of public order disruptions. When approached for comments, HIAL CEO Gitanjali Angmo denied the claims made by the Ladakh administration in its affidavit. Citing a September 25, 2025 order by the Home Ministry cancelling SECMOL's FCRA registration, the affidavit said it was done due to multiple statutory violations which included accepting foreign funds from a Swedish donor to study the sovereignty of the nation deemed prejudicial to national interest. It said that local residents, the Phyang Welfare Society and village Nambardars have repeatedly petitioned authorities since 2018, alleging broken promises regarding the university project, unauthorised diversion of ancient irrigation streams for "Ice Stupa" experiments, and an alleged illegal encroachment of an additional 174 kanals beyond the boundary wall. opening: Leh, Oct 22: The Ladakh administration has defended cancelling land allotment to Sonam Wangchuk's institute, citing the activist's "disregard for the law", and said the allotment automatically lapsed due to unpaid dues and an unexecuted lease deed.

In an affidavit filed in the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, the administration maintained that the 40-year lease allotment covering 1,076 kanals and 1 marla of land at Phyang Thang had "lapsed by operation of law" on May 5, 2019, due to the Himalayan Institute of Alternative Learning (HIAL)'s failure to execute a lease deed or deposit mandatory land premiums within the stipulated one-year period.
body: The affidavit running into 136 pages was filed by Leh Deputy Commissioner and CEO of LAHDC, Romil Singh Donk, in response to HIAL's writ petition challenging the August 21, 2025, cancellation order of leased land to the institute.

The affidavit said the writ petition is "misconceived, devoid of merit, and barred by delay and laches" and made it clear that the original allotment order issued on May 5, 2018, was conditional and explicitly stated that the lease would be deemed cancelled if the allottee failed to execute the deed within a year.
The administration asserted that HIAL never deposited a single rupee towards land premium or ground rent and failed to secure formal possession through the Tehsildar as mandated.

Furthermore, the Higher Education Department of UT Ladakh certified in October 2026 that HIAL is not a recognised university, nor are its courses affiliated with the University of Ladakh or other statutory bodies, violating the core objective of setting up an alternative university.

Bringing other context before the court, the affidavit highlighted the past conduct of HIAL's founder Wangchuk and his organisation, the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL), and said that SECMOL has occupied 124 kanals of state land at Phey for over three decades without formal allotment or payment of an assessed Rs 80 lakh premium.

The affidavit also references the violent protests in Leh in September 2025, which led to Union Home Ministry's intervention, the cancellation of SECMOL's FCRA registration, and Wangchuk's brief detention under the National Security Act prior to its revocation in March 2026, as part of a consistent pattern of public order disruptions.
When approached for comments, HIAL CEO Gitanjali Angmo denied the claims made by the Ladakh administration in its affidavit.

Citing a September 25, 2025 order by the Home Ministry cancelling SECMOL's FCRA registration, the affidavit said it was done due to multiple statutory violations which included accepting foreign funds from a Swedish donor to study the sovereignty of the nation deemed prejudicial to national interest.

It said that local residents, the Phyang Welfare Society and village Nambardars have repeatedly petitioned authorities since 2018, alleging broken promises regarding the university project, unauthorised diversion of ancient irrigation streams for "Ice Stupa" experiments, and an alleged illegal encroachment of an additional 174 kanals beyond the boundary wall.

The affidavit said the villagers complained that HIAL deceived them with false promises of a world-class university, blocked ancient pasture lands, and repeatedly diverted centuries-old natural irrigation streams for Ice Stupa projects, causing severe water shortage for local farmers.

Urging the high court to dismiss the petition, the administration highlighted the antecedents of Wangchuk and SECMOL and submitted that the organisation and the petitioner are merely vehicles through which Wangchuk has repeatedly sought to hold public land on his own terms.
The affidavit also said that HIAL had made false statements under oath in its petition by claiming it sent repeated reminders during the first year and deposited all requisite dues.

It annexed official records showing zero written communications between May 2018 and March 2020, zero payments deposited, and suppressed letters written by HIAL in June 2020 seeking a complete waiver of both premium and ground rent, a request that was never granted.

Tracing official records dating back to 2006, the affidavit pointed out a series of administrative actions and warnings issued against Wangchuk and SECMOL and recalled a October 2006 communication by the then district magistrate of Leh, which recorded that Wangchuk openly threatened the Hill Council and district administration during a council meeting, prompting officials to recommend surveillance and preventive detention.

Official reports from the chief education officer in April 2007 also recorded that Wangchuk had unauthorisedly occupied 200 kanals of land under the guise of educational programmes and disrupted the smooth functioning of the education department.

The administration submitted that this pattern of holding public land without paying state dues continued over the years, including at SECMOL's Phey campus, and has culminated in the present situation where 1,076 kanals of state land have been held for over six years without a valid lease or payment of premium and ground rent.

Linking these past events to broader law and order concerns, the affidavit said that agitations led and incited by Wangchuk in recent years ended with the office of the Chief Executive Councillor of the very Hill Council that originally allotted the land being set on fire.
The administration maintained that a litigant with such a record does not approach the court with clean hands and is not entitled to discretionary or equitable relief.

Dismissing the awards, guest visits, and international recognitions cited by Wangchuk in his petition, the administration said that personal eminence and accolades are wholly irrelevant to the legal question of lease compliance.
